# Bloom filter that rejects codes that never existed

> A Redis-backed Bloom filter that quickly says whether a short code could ever have been created, so lookups for made-up codes stop before the cache or DynamoDB.

_Part of [Look up a code through Bloom filter, cache and DynamoDB](resolve-pipeline.md)_

Short links are looked up by code on every redirect, and people can scan random codes to find links. The Bloom filter is a cheap first guard. It is a compact structure that can say "this code was definitely never created" or "it might exist". It never forgets a real code, but it sometimes says "might exist" for a fake one. The filter is the [`RedisBloomFilter`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/infrastructure/cache/bloom-filter.ts#L12) class, kept in Redis under the key `share-links:bloom`. [`ShareLinkService`](link-click-analytics.md) builds it in its constructor, sized for 100 million codes at a 1% false-positive rate. When `create` stores a new link in DynamoDB, it then calls `bloom.add([code])` to record the code in the filter. When [resolve](resolve-pipeline.md) runs, it checks the code format first. Then it calls `mightContain(code)`. If the answer is no, `resolve` returns `null` at once, with no cache or DynamoDB call. If the answer is yes, the lookup goes on to the cache and DynamoDB. If Redis fails, the `.catch(() => true)` in `resolve` treats the code as "might exist", so real links still work.

**Look at:** [share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts) · [share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts) · [share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts)

## Pieces

- Filter size of 100 million codes at 1% false positives: The constructor creates [`RedisBloomFilter`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/infrastructure/cache/bloom-filter.ts#L12) with the key `share-links:bloom`, a capacity of 100,000,000 and an error rate of 0.01.
- Adding each new code to the filter when a link is created: After the DynamoDB write succeeds, `create` calls `bloom.add` with the new code, so real codes are never rejected.
- Checking the filter before any lookup in resolve: `mightContain` returns false for a code that never existed, and `resolve` then returns `null` without touching the cache or DynamoDB.
- Letting everything through when Redis errors: A `.catch(() => true)` on `mightContain` means a Redis failure acts like "might exist", so the lookup carries on to the cache and DynamoDB.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| cache | `share-links:bloom` | Redis key holding the Bloom filter. `create` adds codes to it and `resolve` checks it with `mightContain`. |
| database | `Links` | DynamoDB table that is only reached when the filter says the code might exist. |

## Also relies on

- [Creating and resolving share links](share-short-links.md): The filter guards the code lookup for `GET /l/:code`, and codes are added to it when links are created.

## Watch out

- The filter can say "might exist" for a code that does not exist. Those codes still go on to the cache and DynamoDB and end up as `null`.
- If Redis is down, the filter lets every code through. During an outage, scans of made-up codes reach DynamoDB.
- The filter is only filled by `create`. A link that is in DynamoDB but was never added to the filter would be rejected as unknown.
- A custom alias is added to the filter too, and `create` clears any cached "not found" for it so the new alias works right away.
